reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the cited text supports it: 20.1 gives an unqualified Vendor defence/indemnity for IP infringement of Services and Deliverables extending to Customer, Affiliates and personnel; 20.2 adds breach of Applicable Law, Customer Data breach caused by Vendor, and gross negligence/wilful misconduct/fraud — matching the model language.

Customer's reverse indemnity (20.3) is appropriately narrow (unmodified Customer-supplied material used as authorised; Customer's own violation of law) with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination and Vendor instructions, satisfying the preferred position's requirement that Customer's indemnity stay narrow.

Standard procedure elements (prompt notice, cooperation at indemnifying party's expense, defence control, consent for prejudicial settlements, prejudice-limited notice failure) are present in 20.4, and 20.5 supplies the procure/modify/replace/terminate-and-refund remedy; deterministic check confirms Vendor IP indemnity present.
Correctly no redline or comment for a compliant finding; the edit-free output is consistent with the claimed status.

Minor rationale inaccuracy (20.4 in fact has the indemnified Party give control of the defence to the indemnifying Party, not retain it), but this is the standard procedure the playbook contemplates and does not change the compliance conclusion.
